clue.text: Copper interrupts confused six-footer

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: confused means lost, bewildered
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman cuts in on a bewildered tall man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. A 'six-footer' here is not a tall person but an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect has six legs, so any insect, including this swarming grasshopper, is a six-footer.

clue.text: Nick, the ultimate in evil, I revile

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

parts.note: to revile is to berate, scold harshly

explanation.surface: A declaration of contempt for the devil and his wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests Old Nick, the devil, but it is a verb: to nick is to steal, and liberate is a jokey euphemism for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for stealing something.

clue.text: Dog on river vessel carrying fuel

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog stands on a river boat carrying fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that carries coal is called a collier.

clue.text: Defective vessel girl observed on lake

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is a vessel
Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl watches a damaged boat on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the normal standard, especially in ability, so lacking.

clue.text: It has a fatal attraction for annoying little types

definitions.text: It has a fatal attraction for annoying little types

parts.words: It has a fatal attraction for annoying little types
parts.note: reads like a femme fatale drawing irritating people, but describes a sticky strip that lures and traps pestering insects

explanation.surface: Someone irresistible proves deadly to tiresome little people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky paper hung up to lure and trap houseflies, which then die stuck to it.

clue.text: Female on stage finding fan troublesome

definitions.text: Female on stage finding fan troublesome

parts.words: Female on stage finding fan troublesome
parts.note: reads like an actress bothered by an admirer, but describes the heroine of an Oscar Wilde play whose fan causes trouble

explanation.surface: An actress is annoyed by an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's comedy is titled after this lady's fan, which, left in the wrong room, causes the scandal of the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Wilde's play, a woman whose fan is the source of the drama.

clue.text: What string may go through to make stitch, might you say?

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: to purl is to make a knitting stitch

explanation.surface: Asking how thread passes through to form a stitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearls are drilled so a string can be threaded through for a necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem from an oyster, drilled and threaded on a string to make a necklace.

clue.text: After storm is a crop flat?

indicators.note: after a storm things are tossed about, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Is a crop of wheat lying flattened after a storm?
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and prosaic both mean dull, lacking imagination.

clue.text: Iscariot erred — covert member of the mob?

indicators.note: covert means concealed, so the letters lurk inside the words

explanation.surface: Judas made a mistake: was he secretly one of the crowd?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in a riot is part of a disorderly crowd.

clue.text: Never hate a boss violently — keep prudently silent

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Advice not to loathe your manager fiercely, and to say nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means not to bother speaking because it would be pointless.

clue.text: Fellow showing no interest, we hear, in poster site

parts.note: Bill is a man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: the phrase signals that a word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: someone showing no interest is bored

explanation.surface: A man looks uninterested in the spot where a poster is displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor hoarding on which advertisements are pasted is a site for posters.

clue.text: It's almost over, love, from the outset

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: over in the sense of higher than means above
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A match is nearly finished, love having been there from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: AB OVO is Latin, literally 'from the egg', meaning from the very beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means starting from the egg, hence right from the beginning.

clue.text: Cereal's natural 'abitat reported to suit underground stem

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: rye is a cereal and its natural home, with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows, is 'ome

explanation.surface: A grain's native habitat is described as suitable for a root-like stem.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''abitat' tells you to drop it from 'home' too: 'rye's 'ome' said quickly sounds like the botanical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call a horizontal stem growing below the soil, like that of ginger or iris, by this name.

clue.text: Is this Scot a star in the Eton game?

parts.note: the Wall Game is a ball game played only at Eton College
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A question whether a Scottish man excels at an English school sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton Wall Game is a muddy, rarely-scoring football game peculiar to Eton, an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace was the Scottish patriot who led resistance to English rule, and the surname is Scottish.

clue.text: Play idly with loose thread

definitions.meaning: to strum or drum the fingers idly on an instrument or table
the fringe of unwoven threads left at the end of a weaving warp

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to strum idly and a loose warp end left on a loom.

clue.text: An hour in church, superior church that is unrivalled

parts.note: Nones is one of the canonical hours of daily prayer, said at the ninth hour
U stands for upper-class, hence superior

explanation.surface: Time spent in a grand church that has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Nones is the monastic office of mid-afternoon. U is a British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person or thing without equal, a paragon; here used attributively for matchless.

clue.text: Term a witty person undermining Society a scamp

indicators.note: in a down clue, undermining means placed beneath, so the following pieces come after

parts.note: to term is to call, name
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: Calling a joker a rogue weakens society.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal, an old spelling of scallywag.

clue.text: Successive notes finished and kept in safe place

parts.note: D, E and F are consecutive musical notes
finished means ended

explanation.surface: A sequence of music concluded and was stored securely.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarded or protected, so kept out of harm.

clue.text: Man once in the country? Man perhaps in the city

parts.note: carl is an old word for a churl, a countryman
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: Asking about a rustic of old, then about someone in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland. Carlisle is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is an English cathedral city near the Scottish border.

clue.text: Information attorney brought in when making lists

indicators.note: brought in places pieces inside another

parts.note: as means when
gen is slang for information
DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer's data is used to compile lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Monkey with small place inside tree

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another here

parts.note: an ape is loosely a monkey
PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A monkey has a little spot within a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit-bearing tree of orchards shares its name with the fruit.

clue.text: Rank smell comes from medicine of dubious value

parts.note: rank means place in order
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: An offensive odour comes from questionable medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective for a smell, but it is a noun meaning position.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Suppressed writer nominated

annotationWithheld.why: Suppressed writer nominated (4-2): PEN for writer plus PUT UP for nominated gives PENPUTUP, not PENTUP; no parse found and a search gave nothing

clue.text: English parson may provide uplift

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: An English clergyman might offer spiritual elevation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplift' suggests spiritual comfort from the parson, but it means something that raises things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sets up or raises a structure literally gives it lift.

clue.text: Is repulsive creature turning up bones?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a rat is a creature many find repulsive

explanation.surface: Is a nasty animal showing its bones?
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the bones of the ankle.

clue.text: The distance travelled in a race against time

parts.note: the mile is a classic athletics race
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: How far one runs in a race against the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The total number of miles covered by a vehicle or traveller.

clue.text: Like some old houses you found abroad attracting beetle

parts.note: tu is French for you
a dor is a dung beetle

explanation.surface: An old house where you find beetles when overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Tudor houses are half-timbered English buildings from the 1500s.
explanation.definitionFit: The style of house built in the Tudor period of English history, 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Cockney school principal offers a tip

parts.note: Harrow is a famous school, and a Cockney drops the H
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A London headmaster gives some advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are held to drop initial H. Harrow is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed head of an arrow is its tip.

clue.text: It's cheap, nasty imitation

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissal of some cheap and unpleasant copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A work that imitates the style of another artist is a pastiche.

clue.text: A lodge needs restoration, being ancient

indicators.note: restoring here means rebuilding the letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An old lodge is in need of repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for ages is very old.
